name: Metal2Humanoid
tagline: Building a Humanoid Robot from the Ground Up
description: Metal2Humanoid is a proposed non-credit MIT IAP 2027 course: a four-week, hands-on introduction to humanoid robotics, from motors and actuators to coordinated motion and learned behavior, built on an open-source humanoid.

status.approvalNote: Proposed as a non-credit MIT IAP 2027 activity; approval, meeting times, and rooms are provisional.

registration.label: Register
registration.note: Registration is not open yet. Details will be posted here once the offering is approved and scheduled.

hbrn.name: Homebrew Robotics Network
hbrn.relationship: Metal2Humanoid is organized by its instructors together with members of the Homebrew Robotics Network (HBRN), the builder community behind the initiative.
hbrn.blurb: The Homebrew Robotics Network is a community of builders working toward open, accessible, reproducible robotics: hardware that can be built from widely available parts, documented well enough for others to repeat, and shared under open licenses. Its members contribute builds, documentation, testing, and teaching.
hbrn.next: Beyond the IAP course, HBRN is exploring two companion efforts that may extend the course materials: OSH Atlas, an atlas of open humanoid projects and resources, and UMOJA, a framework for assessing and comparing open humanoid designs. Both are possible future extensions for documentation, resource sharing, and benchmarking. Neither is a deliverable of the course.
